\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تعمیرگاه} (ta'mirgâh)}{تعمیرگاه (ta'mirgâh)}]{\fa{تعمیرگاه} (ta'mirgâh) — a garage, a repair shop}

\label{lesson:FA-C427-tamirgah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for one-way, then the Persian for a driving licence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تعمیرگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{تعمیرگاه}} (\emph{ta'mirgâh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a garage, a repair shop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ماشین} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{تعمیرگاه} \fa{بردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâshin râ be ta'mirgâh bordim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We took the car to the garage.
\end{quote}

\emph{ta'mir} 'repair' + \emph{gâh} 'place'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'mirgâh} is built from \emph{ta'mir} 'repair', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{taʿmīr} 'making habitable, restoring', and the native \emph{gâh} 'place'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'mirgâh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'mirgâh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ta'mirgâh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for one-way, then the Persian for a driving licence, then say \emph{ta'mirgâh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{تعمیرگاه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A garage, a repair shop\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تعمیر} \fa{کردن} (ta'mir kardan)}{تعمیر کردن (ta'mir kardan)}]{\fa{تعمیر} \fa{کردن} (ta'mir kardan) — to repair, to fix}

\label{lesson:FA-C427-tamir-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a driving licence, then the Persian for a garage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تعمیر} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تعمیر} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ta'mir kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to repair, to fix\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مکانیک} \fa{ماشین} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{دو} \fa{روز} \fa{تعمیر} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mekânik mâshin râ dar do ruz ta'mir kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mechanic repaired the car in two days.
\end{quote}

\emph{ta'mir} + \emph{kardan}. Present stem \emph{kon-}: \emph{ta'mir mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ta'mir kardan} is built from \emph{ta'mir} 'repair', usually traced to Arabic \emph{taʿmīr} 'restoring', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'mir kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ta'mir kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ta'mir kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a driving licence, then the Persian for a garage, then say \emph{ta'mir kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{تعمیر} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To repair, to fix\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جوش} \fa{آوردن} (jush âvardan)}{جوش آوردن (jush âvardan)}]{\fa{جوش} \fa{آوردن} (jush âvardan) — to overheat (of an engine); to boil over; to lose your temper}

\label{lesson:FA-C427-jush-avardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a garage, then the Persian for to repair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جوش} \fa{آوردن}}
\textbf{\fa{جوش} \fa{آوردن}} (\emph{jush âvardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to overheat (of an engine); to boil over; to lose your temper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{گرمای} \fa{تابستان} \fa{ماشین} \fa{ما} \fa{جوش} \fa{آورد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar garmâ-ye tâbestân mâshin-e mâ jush âvard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the summer heat our car overheated.
\end{quote}

\emph{jush} 'boiling' + \emph{âvardan} 'to bring'. Said of people too: \emph{jush âvard} — he lost his temper.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jush âvardan} is built from \emph{jush} 'boiling, simmering', a native word that EtymDB lists, and \emph{âvardan} 'to bring', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{āwurdan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jush âvardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jush âvardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{jush âvardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a garage, then the Persian for to repair, then say \emph{jush âvardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{جوش} \fa{آوردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To overheat (of an engine); to boil over; to lose your temper\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{یدک} \fa{کش} (yadakkesh)}{یدک کش (yadakkesh)}]{\fa{یدک} \fa{کش} (yadakkesh) — a tow truck, a breakdown lorry}

\label{lesson:FA-C427-yadakkesh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to repair, then the Persian for to overheat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{یدک} \fa{کش}}
\textbf{\fa{یدک} \fa{کش}} (\emph{yadakkesh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a tow truck, a breakdown lorry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{یدک} \fa{کش} \fa{ماشین} \fa{ما} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{تعمیرگاه} \fa{برد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Yadakkesh mâshin-e mâ râ be ta'mirgâh bord.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The tow truck took our car to the garage.
\end{quote}

\emph{yadak} 'spare, in tow' + \emph{kesh} 'puller', from \emph{keshidan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{yadakkesh} is built from \emph{yadak} 'a led horse, a spare', usually traced to a Turkic word for a horse led on a rope, and \emph{kesh} 'puller', from the native verb \emph{keshidan} 'to pull'. EtymDB lists neither part.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yadakkesh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yadakkesh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{yadakkesh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to repair, then the Persian for to overheat, then say \emph{yadakkesh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{یدک} \fa{کش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tow truck, a breakdown lorry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بکسل} \fa{کردن} (boksel kardan)}{بکسل کردن (boksel kardan)}]{\fa{بکسل} \fa{کردن} (boksel kardan) — to tow}

\label{lesson:FA-C427-boksel-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to overheat, then the Persian for a tow truck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بکسل} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بکسل} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{boksel kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to tow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرم} \fa{ماشین} \fa{خراب} \fa{مرا} \fa{با} \fa{طناب} \fa{بکسل} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâdaram mâshin-e kharâb-e marâ bâ tanâb boksel kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother towed my broken-down car with a rope.
\end{quote}

\emph{boksel} (a tow rope) + \emph{kardan}. Present stem \emph{kon-}: \emph{boksel mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{boksel kardan} is built from \emph{boksel} 'a tow, a tow rope', which EtymDB takes from Russian \emph{buksír} 'towing', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
